clarity: I knew the next floor I wanted, but I initially mistook the ration button's 'ok $650' for a completed purchase and only later confirmed it.
decisions: I accepted 'D23 38→0%' to try a safe cash farm for the overnight return, and would make that choice again only when money mattered more than a new floor.
mastery: I can now put a specific threat ahead of the nearest enemy, and the next run actually showed 'hit drain wraith' before those enemies could keep shaving my maximum health.
tension: The Master fight caught me at '6/42 hp' while new carry was at risk, and the final healing recovery made its defeat a relief.
feel: Menu selections answered promptly and big hit numbers were easy to see, but repeated 'REST ✗ NOT SAFE' bubbles kept drawing my eye away from the actual blows; I could not listen to audio.
surprise: The learned 'iron golem · reflects melee' made me keep the reflector tactic for the foundry instead of treating every enemy as another nearest-target fight.
expression: My adventurer is a guarded rogue who tries an unknown scroll in danger and hunts draining enemies first, with '2/4 rules' sitting above the supplied packages.
story: After 'grudge: Ulak the ghoul' marked Jora's killer, I sent Kael with draining enemies first, watched him kill Ulak and the Lich, and saw him survive the Master before reaching D25.
pacing: The 'D9–12 swift · 100%' fold cut familiar travel, but later ordinary fights still repeated for minutes; my return visits gave distinct preparation choices while the expanded ledgers took sustained reading.
failure: Jora lost because I left nearest attacks ahead of the draining enemy while healing was empty and 'to corridor vs 3+ · no path ← foes hold the way' ruled out my escape plan.
social: I played alone; 'Ulusk · old hound · served Hale, Iris, Jora' gave the town a continuing name, without another person or a developing conversation.
autonomy: I switched away from the starting fighter to a rogue and later pursued safe cash before depth, even though the town still pointed me toward 'Goal D23'.
progression: The rogue's levels, bigger pack and new floor vocabulary stayed available between heirs, and 'scout · sent 10' meant I no longer had to initiate every expedition myself.
aesthetic: Torchlit stone, parchment reports and the line 'Slag with silver in it.' made the dungeon inviting to look at, although packed grey figures and oversized control panels sometimes obscured the scene; audio is unassessed.
return: After four hours I came back to the Lich beaten, an heir lost and 'apprentice · +2 steps → pack 5', so I studied the gas death and changed preparation rather than wishing I had stayed to tap sends.
attribution: I credit my extra healing slot for the last 'heal potion · +21 HP' in the Master fight, while the automatic reflector package and personality changes mean I cannot claim every winning blow as my own authored instruction.
